segments.narration: Skeletons hang thousands of feet above the jungle floor. Deep in the Peruvian cloud forest, jagged limestone cliffs hide hundreds of ancient wooden sarcophagi.
Long before the Inca empire conquered the Andes, the elusive Chachapoyas civilization ruled these misty peaks. Why did they haul massive stone blocks and entire bodies to impossible vertical heights?
They weren't just hiding from rival armies. These cliffside tombs, painted with ochre geometric symbols, were meant to bridge the gap between the living world and the realm of the ancestors.
For centuries, looters stripped the most accessible sites bare, leaving behind scattered bones and shattered pottery. Archaeologists feared the ultimate secret of the Cliff People was lost forever.

Then, a fog-shrouded burial site at Laguna de los Cóndores revealed over two hundred mummies completely undisturbed. Protected by the freezing, dry microclimate of the overhang, their elaborate wrappings and funerary bundles finally proved how deeply these masters of the heights revered their dead.
